anomalies.observed: On the MCU sheet the USB-C receptacle J3 pin A4 (the USB VBUS pin) is connected to BOTH the '+5V' power symbol and the 'VBUS' global label. On the power sheet '+5V' is the TPS2121 (U11) IN2 pin and 'VBUS' is the U11 OUT pin / buck (U7) input. Because J3.A4 carries both labels, the +5V net and the VBUS net are merged into one net, so the mux's IN2 and OUT end up on the same rail and the USB supply is hard-wired to the internal pre-buck rail.
anomalies.expected: The spec keeps these two rails separate: 'IN2 (pin 2) wired to USB +5V/VBUS, with a common OUT feeding the board's unregulated VBUS rail ... note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux', and lists the power mux as a headline protection decision ('a power mux (not a diode-OR) arbitrates the two possible input supplies'). J3.A4 should be on +5V only, feeding U11 IN2; VBUS should be U11 OUT only.

anomalies.impact: The TPS2121 power mux is bypassed: its IN2 and OUT are shorted together and the USB 5V pin is tied directly to the internal VBUS rail. When the 12 V barrel jack is connected, the mux output (~12 V) is driven back onto the USB VBUS pin, back-powering the host port and risking damage; the intended seamless 12 V/5 V arbitration is lost.
